In 2026, keyword research has transitioned from a volume-chasing numbers game into a strategic system focused on **solving user problems and mapping topical entities** [1, 2]. The process now serves two distinct audiences: human searchers and AI retrieval agents [3].

### 1. Finding Keywords: Discovery Tactics
The discovery phase requires mining five distinct data sources to reveal opportunities that single-method approaches miss [4].

*   **Topic Definition & AI Ideation:** Start with 5–10 core topics your business must own [5]. Use AI assistants (ChatGPT or Claude) for ideation by prompting them to list questions a target audience might ask about those subjects [6].
*   **Seed Keyword Expansion:** Brainstorm broad stems and add modifiers like "best," "how to," or "vs" [7, 8].
*   **Competitor Intelligence:** Export rankings from the top 10 results of your primary topics [9]. Semrush research suggests that competitive gap analysis can discover **342% more opportunities** than standard keyword expansion [4].
*   **Owned Data Mining:** Use **Google Search Console (GSC)** to find queries you already rank for but haven't optimized. Focus on long-tail, conversational queries that third-party tools often miss [6, 10].
*   **Voice & Conversational Sources:** Mine **Google Autocomplete**, **"People Also Ask" (PAA)** boxes, and follow-up questions proposed in AI interfaces to capture natural language patterns [6, 11, 12].

### 2. Reliability of Metrics: Volume and Difficulty
In 2026, search volume and keyword difficulty (KD) are treated as **directional indicators rather than absolute facts** [13, 14].

*   **Search Volume Accuracy:** Industry research indicates that volume estimates vary **15–30% between major tools**, with individual keywords showing discrepancies as high as 60% [15, 16]. High volume no longer guarantees high traffic due to **zero-click AI Overviews**, which now appear in approximately **25% to 50% of searches** [17, 18].
*   **Keyword Difficulty Conflicts:** Tools use vastly different formulas. For the same keyword, **Ahrefs KD** might be 65 (focusing on backlinks) while **Semrush KD** is 25 (weighing SERP features and domain diversity) [19].
*   **Recommended Thresholds:** New sites (Domain Authority under 20) are advised to target **KD scores under 20** for "quick wins" achievable within 3–6 months [20, 21].
*   **Verification Tactic:** Never trust tool labels blindly. **Manual KD assessment** is required: compare your site's authority against the top 10 average; if the gap is massive, the keyword is likely unreachable regardless of the tool's score [22-24].

### 3. Classifying Search Intent
Classifying intent is the mandatory starting point before looking at metrics [25, 26].

*   **The Four Traditional Buckets:** Informational (Learn), Navigational (Go), Commercial (Compare), and Transactional (Do) [25].
*   **The 2026 Informational Split:** Informational intent is now split into **"Shallow"** (resolved by a quick AI paragraph) and **"Deep"** (requires methodology, judgment, or expert trust) [27]. Clicks are holding up best for Deep Informational and Commercial queries [28].
*   **SERP Analysis Workflow:** Search the keyword in an incognito window. If the top 10 are all product pages, a blog post will not rank [29, 30]. **Match the dominant content format** the algorithm has already validated for that specific query [30, 31].

### 4. Keyword Clustering Methodology
The unit of modern research is the **cluster**, not the individual keyword [32].

*   **The "One Page Per Intent" Rule:** Group related queries that share a primary intent and can be answered by a single page [33].
*   **Clustering by SERP Overlap:** Keywords belong in the same cluster if the search engine returns **60% or more of the same URLs** for both terms [32, 34].
*   **Pillar and Cluster Model:** Build a comprehensive "pillar" page for a broad head term, supported by 10–20 "cluster" pages targeting subtopics and follow-up questions [35-37].

### 5. Content Gap Analysis
Content gap analysis identifies keywords where competitors rank in the top 3, but your site does not appear in the top 20 [38, 39].

*   **Audit Workflow:** Use tools like Ahrefs Content Gap or Semrush Keyword Gap to compare your domain against **3–5 competitors simultaneously** [9, 39].
*   **Validated Demand:** Prioritize subtopics covered by **two or more competitors** that you lack, as this confirms Google is actively rewarding that specific coverage [40].

### 6. The AI Shift: Query Fan-Out and Passage Optimization
Keyword research has changed because AI search engines now "consume your website for the user" rather than just sending them there [41].

*   **The Fan-Out Phenomenon:** AI engines expand a single prompt into an average of **9–11 sub-queries** (sometimes up to 28) behind the scenes [42, 43]. These "synthetic" sub-queries often have zero search volume because humans never type them [44].
*   **Passage-Level Retrieval:** Search engines now retrieve and rank **passages (40–200 words)** rather than just whole pages [45, 46].
*   **The "BID" Formula (Ahrefs-specific methodology):** Evaluate every keyword for **Business potential**, **Intent**, and **Difficulty** [93–95].
*   **The AI Filter Tactic:** Before committing, ask: **"Can AI fully satisfy the user for this query?"** [47]. If the AI overview nails the answer, that keyword may be a "trap" for traditional organic clicks and should instead be targeted for **AI citation** [47, 48].
*   **Structure for Extraction:** Structure content so every H2 is a searchable question followed by a **40–60 word answer block** containing your brand name and a specific data point; this format is 30–40% more likely to be cited by AI [49-51].

Semantic clustering — grouping by shared words or embedding similarity — fails in exactly the cases that matter. Queries about a service's cost and queries about hiring for that service can read as near-identical text while representing different searchers at different stages, with different SERPs to match. The second source is the people who talk to your customers. Sales calls, support tickets, intake forms, and the exact wording prospects use to describe their problem are keyword research in its purest form — these are the questions that get asked when a real budget is attached. The phrasing your sales team hears every week is the phrasing being typed into search boxes and asked of assistants, usually long before it shows volume anywhere.

The second shift is that the biggest-volume queries are precisely the ones losing clicks. Broad informational searches — definitions, how-it-works questions, simple comparisons — are increasingly answered directly on the results page by AI-generated summaries, or never reach a search engine at all because the user asked an assistant instead. The volume is still reported. The click that volume used to imply is, for many of those queries, no longer there to win.

How do you calculate keyword difficulty manually?

Treat KD scores with extreme caution. Most third-party tools calculate difficulty almost entirely based on the backlink profiles of the top-ranking pages. They do not account for content quality, semantic depth, topical authority, or how well a page satisfies user intent. Use KD as a rough filter, but always manually verify the true difficulty by analyzing the actual SERP.
